comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C108-C110 regarding K125E structures in HEPES buffer without CO2. Both evaluations support that K125E biases conformation independently of CO2, though acknowledge lower resolution and potential additional CO2 effects. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C72-C78 describing correlated conformational changes involving TM1 rotation and Trp24 movements. Both evaluations support the structural observations with quantitative evidence. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C56, C125-C130 regarding pore-occupying density. However, OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED while peer review marks as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval emphasizes evidence against detergent and biological relevance, while peer reviewers note the functional role remains speculative and lacks clear explanation.

Perfect alignment on claims C69, C139-C147 regarding the lack of definitive K125-R104 interaction. Both evaluations mark as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging insufficient EM density to support direct interaction and the speculative nature of the proposed salt bridge mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C153-C157 connecting structural findings to disease mechanisms (A88V and R143W mutations). Both evaluations support the structural rationale for disease phenotypes. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C49-C68 regarding improved structural resolution through detergent optimization and visualization of cytoplasmic loop. Both evaluations praise this technical achievement and mark as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers highlighting this as a major strength.

Both address K125E functional data (C4, C91-C94) showing constitutive closure. OpenEval focuses specifically on dye transfer assays, while peer review integrates this with broader structural evidence (C5, C52, C95, C100-C107, C135, C144). Both mark as SUPPORTED with unanimous reviewer praise.

Substantial overlap on claims about K125E conformational bias (C5, C52, C95, C100-C107). OpenEval emphasizes particle distribution and structural similarity to closed state. Peer review integrates these with functional data and broader mechanistic context. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both address conformational selection and lack of subunit cooperativity (C131-C133). OpenEval includes additional claims about correlation with functional data (C134, C151). Both evaluations support the conformational selection model. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on lack of cooperativity (C87-C89). OpenEval focuses on single-subunit classification limitations and structural flexibility. Peer review emphasizes incompatibility with C6-symmetric arrangement and contrast with hemichannel cooperativity. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on cytoplasmic loop structure (C113-C117, C119). OpenEval emphasizes comparative analysis across connexin family and KVRIEG motif matching AlphaFold2. Peer review focuses on successful visualization and AlphaFold validation. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on KVRIEG motif and AlphaFold2 validation (C113-C115). OpenEval synthesizes broader regulatory mechanism (C9, C10, C51, C112, C160). Peer review focuses on cytoplasmic loop visualization achievement. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on K125R structural data (C98, C99, C101). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED emphasizing conformational bias evidence. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting K125R results were 'inconclusive' and less definitive than K125E data.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic synthesis (C160). OpenEval integrates structural observations into regulatory mechanism. Peer review provides overall assessment of mechanism support with acknowledgment that further studies are needed for specific details. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on conformational selection model (C151). OpenEval focuses on conformational selection vs induced fit with functional correlation. Peer review provides broader assessment of overall mechanism. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on integration of prior work (C135, C144). OpenEval addresses K125E mimicry of carbamylation and structural proximity evidence (C3, C35-C43, C136-C138). Peer review includes these in broader support for central mechanism. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C1-C34) as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations to established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.

OpenEval evaluates novelty of cytoplasmic loop density observation (C7, C8, C28, C62-C66) as SUPPORTED. While peer reviewers praise this achievement (covered in R2), no separate peer evaluation specifically addresses the novelty claims.
OpenEval evaluates previous functional studies on K125 mutations (C44-C47, C90) as SUPPORTED based on citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature summary claims.
OpenEval evaluates limitations of prior work (C48) as SUPPORTED, motivating current study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific motivational claim.

OpenEval evaluates honest reporting of structural modeling limitations (C58, C79, C83, C84, C104) as SUPPORTED. While peer reviewers acknowledge limitations, no separate evaluation specifically addresses these limitation statements.

Minimal overlap on disease relevance (C161). OpenEval focuses specifically on structural rationale for disease mutations (C153-C159). Peer review provides general assessment that study offers structural insights for disease understanding. Both mark as SUPPORTED.
